newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower, Eurotunnel rises.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower, Eurotunnel rises.

text.p: French shares started lower on continued profit-taking after recent highs and on worries an ongoing truckers' strike could spread and damage the economy.

Eurotunnel bounced back on Wednesday, after an almost uninterrupted slide since the November 18 fire, following a declaration by co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle that the operator would suffer no financial impact from the fire.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 5.25 points or 0.23 percent at 2,269.83 at 0912 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,273 from 2,275 on Tuessay's close.
Eurotunnel was up 4.65 pct at 6.75 francs.
Volume was 680 million francs of which 510 million was on the CAC-40 stocks at around 0930 GMT.
Elf was the busiest stock. The oil group said its nine month sales had increased to 167.725 billion francs from 156.212 billion, with nearly half of the increase being posted in the third quarter.

Alcatel Alsthom down 1.32 percent to 456 francs on statements by chairman Serge Tchuruk, made to a pariliamentary commission last week but published on Tuesday, that his company is willing to renew its bid for Thomson SA after the December 31 expiry date for the Lagardere bid.

GEC chairman Lord Weinstock told Les Echos he was ready to talk with whoever acquired Thomson about merging Marconi with Thomson-CSF. Weinstock also said he was willing to pay "a dowry" to keep 50 percent of an enlarged GEC-Alsthom Framatome company. Alcatel would stand to get part of the money because it would bring its 44 percent stake in Framatome to the enlarged group.

Lagardere down 0.58 percent at 154.10 francs. Stock market watchdog COB declined to comment on a report it had started an investigation in trading in Lagardere shares just prior to the news its bid was selected by the government as the preferable offer for Thomson.
